title: From Space to Success: An Exploration of Interior Design Practices for Optimal Learning Outcomes in Higher Education

findings.antecedent: Natural light sources (daylighting) and outdoor views in classrooms
findings.consequent: Cognitive performance, student well-being, focus, productivity
findings.quote: Research suggests that in daylighted classrooms, math scores improve by up to 20% and verbal scores by up to 22% (Fielding, 2006).

findings.consequent: Electricity consumption, cooling load, institutional sustainability
findings.quote: Additionally, daylighting efforts can reduce the amount of electricity a facility uses by allowing users to keep electric lights turned off during the day. The reduction in electricity consumption is furthered by the reduction in the cooling load required by the facility. This is because the efficient utilization of daylighting allows for passive heating to occur (Samani, 2011).

findings.antecedent: Excessive levels of noise, reverberation, and poor sound insulation in learning environments
findings.consequent: Learning activities, concentration, information retention, distraction
findings.quote: Excessive levels of noise, reverberation, and poor sound insulation can ultimately hinder learning activities and contribute to distraction.

findings.antecedent: Improved Indoor Air Quality (IAQ) and 'greener' indoor environments
findings.consequent: Employee productivity, sick days, allergies, asthma, sick building syndrome (SBS)
findings.quote: After surveying 2,000 workers, researchers found that improving the IAQ could increase productivity by 4.8% and reduce sick days by 3 per year. The same researchers found that “greener” indoor environments could reduce allergies and asthma by 8%-25%, and reduce symptoms of sick building syndrome (SBS) by 9%-20%.

findings.antecedent: Spatial layouts and technological integration (when done well)
findings.consequent: Active learning environments, diverse teaching/learning styles, dynamic engagement, interaction between instructor and student, participation
findings.quote: When done well, they can promote active learning environments and support diverse teaching and learning styles. Flexible classroom configurations, adaptable furniture, and collaborative workspaces all encourage dynamic engagement, interaction between instructor and student, and participation in one's own educational journey.

findings.antecedent: Traditional lecture hall style classrooms (large groups, limited instruction space)
findings.consequent: Student retention, overall satisfaction, participation, social interaction, likelihood of failure
findings.quote: National attrition rates have remained alarmingly high for years, with only 55% of students successfully completing their degree within six years at public higher education institutions. The common practice of herding large groups of students into lecture halls with one to two hundred other students may be partially to blame for these rates. Large class sizes have been shown to be associated with lower student retention and overall satisfaction with the course.

findings.consequent: Student responsibility in education, test scores
findings.quote: Research has found that students placed in a lecture-style classroom are 1.5 times more likely to fail than those being taught in more active learning settings. The same study suggested that active learning techniques can improve test scores by 6%.

findings.antecedent: Group study areas (with flexible furniture, power integration)
findings.consequent: Teamwork, effective collaboration, knowledge sharing, accommodation of different group sizes and learning activities
findings.quote: Flexible furniture pieces and arrangements, easily moveable furniture, furniture with power integration, all can enhance the effectiveness of a group study area by accommodating different group sizes and learning activities (Wu et al., 2021).

findings.antecedent: Flexibility of a physical learning space
findings.quote: the flexibility of a physical space can affect teachers' ways of teaching; when in a more flexible space, teachers emphasize the use of more student-centered practices (Teemu Valtonen et al., 2020).

findings.antecedent: Biophilic design elements (greenery, daylighting, outdoor views, natural materials, colors)
findings.consequent: Stress, mood, cognitive function among students
findings.quote: Research demonstrates that biophilic design elements can actually reduce stress, improve mood, and enhance cognitive function among students.

findings.antecedent: Design elements (including biophilic design, personalized spaces, branding, flexible furniture, study nooks, communal areas)
findings.consequent: Place attachment, sense of belonging, restorative environment, sense of ownership, identity, visceral connection to institution
findings.quote: Even biophilic design elements have been shown to facilitate these bonds, because they help create a restorative environment. Restorative environments do not necessarily have to be natural or include natural elements, but they do tend to rate higher when looking at place attachments (Gillis & Gatersleben, 2015).

findings.antecedent: Warm colors (yellow, orange) in interior design
findings.consequent: Energy, creativity, optimism, congestion, overstimulation, fear (yellow)
findings.quote: Research suggests that warm colors like yellow and orange can promote energy, creativity, and optimism, while cool colors like blue or green can evoke relaxation and focus. Using warm colors can also accentuate something, but overusing them can lead to a space appearing congested.

findings.antecedent: Cool colors (blue, green) in interior design
findings.consequent: Relaxation, focus, breathing speed, blood pressure, concentration
findings.quote: Cool colors can also influence the nervous system, by reducing breathing speed and blood pressure, so they can be placed freely where designers want to create a calming effect... Blue is calming for the central nervous system, it tends to increase concentration (Ćurĉić, A. et al., 2019).
Research shows that red is the most stimulating color, and can attract immediate attention. It should be used sparingly throughout interior spaces to avoid a compacted look.
